site.description: Visit Chew Jetty on Weld Quay, George Town: listed opening hours, free general entry, directions, clan jetty heritage and respectful visiting tips.

hero.title: Chew Jetty
hero.subtitle: Chew Jetty is one of the surviving Chinese clan jetties in George Town, Penang. Its wooden boardwalk stretching into the sea, stilt houses, and red lanterns make it a must-visit destination.

intro.title: A Heritage Water Village
intro.p1: Chew Jetty is a living waterfront neighbourhood on Weld Quay in George Town, Penang. Explore the public wooden walkways while respecting the stilt homes and residents.
intro.p2: Penang’s official tourism directory lists Chew Jetty at 59A, Chew Jetty, Weld Quay. It is one of George Town’s clan jetties, within the historic waterfront area.
bullets: A living witness to Hokkien Chinese immigrant history
Stilt houses, a shrine and souvenir stalls
A residential waterfront to explore respectfully
intro.imgAlt: Buildings and walkway on Chew Jetty, 30 April 2024

history.title: History & Heritage
history.intro: Chew Jetty belongs to George Town’s historic waterfront. The official tourism directory introduces it as part of the clan jetty visitor area.

timeline.title: George Town’s clan jetties
timeline.text: Chew Jetty is one of the clan jetties on Weld Quay. The homes and shared walkways form part of the waterfront’s living community.

timeline.title: George Town’s World Heritage context
timeline.text: UNESCO lists Melaka and George Town together as the Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca. This recognition provides context for exploring George Town’s historic neighbourhoods.

timeline.title: A residential community
timeline.text: People live and work here. Keep to public paths, leave doorways clear and follow residents’ instructions.

fireUpdate.title: Visiting hours & what to check
fireUpdate.intro: Google Maps lists Chew Jetty as 09:00–21:00 on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday; Thursday is 09:00–21:30.
points: The Penang tourism directory for the wider Clan Jetties area lists 11:00–21:00 daily. This covers the group of jetties rather than the exact Chew Jetty listing.
Use the specific Chew Jetty listing as a planning reference and follow signs, residents’ instructions and any closures on arrival. Individual shops can keep different hours.
General admission is listed as free on Google Maps. Purchases, tours and other services may cost extra.
Do not assume 24-hour visitor access. Chew Jetty is a residential neighbourhood; private homes and restricted areas are not visitor routes.
fireUpdate.note: Sources checked 19 October 2026. This independent guide distinguishes the specific Chew Jetty listing from the wider Clan Jetties area. Recheck hours and access before travel.

folkFaith.title: Beliefs & Traditional Festivals
folkFaith.intro: Religious observances belong to the community. Public access and visitor arrangements depend on the community’s plans for the year.

items.title: Pai Thian Kong — Birthday of the Jade Emperor
items.text: If you hope to observe Pai Thian Kong celebrations, check current community announcements for dates, access and visitor guidance. Do not assume a public programme or a particular ceremony.

items.title: Shrine at the end of the jetty
items.text: Shrines are places of worship. Follow local instructions, keep noise down and ask before taking photos.

items.title: Hungry Ghost Festival
items.text: For Hungry Ghost Festival observances, check the community’s arrangements for the year. Keep worship areas clear and ask before photographing rituals.

items.title: Chinese New Year & Chap Goh Meh
items.text: Check the year’s community or official event announcements for Chinese New Year and Chap Goh Meh. Fireworks, processions and public programmes are not guaranteed.

architecture.title: Stilt House Architecture
architecture.intro: The raised homes and shared wooden walkways form a distinctive waterfront neighbourhood. Keep to public paths and leave entrances clear.

features.title: Wooden pillars into the seabed
features.text: Houses are raised on wooden pillars driven directly into the seabed. During high tide, the water level can rise to almost the floor level of the houses.

features.title: Interwoven wooden walkways
features.text: Shared wooden walkways connect the waterfront homes. Follow posted access restrictions and avoid blocking narrow sections.

features.title: A complete community space
features.text: On the jetty one finds a shrine, stalls, clothes-drying areas, washing areas, and a boat mooring — a complete village floating on water.

features.title: Heritage conservation
features.text: As part of a World Heritage Site, any renovation and repair is subject to the conservation guidelines of George Town World Heritage Incorporated to preserve its original character.

film.title: Photography & the Waterfront
film.intro: Enjoy the waterfront from public routes while respecting the people who live here.

sites.title: Views from public paths
sites.text: Photograph the waterfront and streetscape only from permitted public areas. Do not enter homes or seek access to private interiors.

sites.title: Photographing people & worship
sites.text: Ask permission before taking close-up photos of residents or religious activities. Follow signs and any instructions on site.

bestTime.title: Best Time & Visit Tips
bestTime.intro: Chew Jetty offers a different atmosphere throughout the day. Mornings are good for quiet photos, while late afternoons offer beautiful sunset light.

periods.description: Lower crowd levels, ideal for photos of the wooden boardwalk without the crowds. The weather is also more comfortable.
Shops and food stalls are busy, but the weather may be hot. Do bring a hat and sunscreen.
Choose a late-afternoon visit for changing light over the waterfront. A clear sunset view depends on weather, viewpoint and permitted access.

bestTime.duration: 1 – 2 hours is enough for a leisurely walk, photos, and an afternoon drink by the water.

food.title: Chew Jetty Street Food & Food Nearby
food.intro: Don't miss the chance to try Penang's iconic dishes before or after visiting the jetty.

spots.name: Penang Asam Laksa
spots.description: Penang’s sour, fish-based asam laksa is one option to look for while exploring George Town. Check individual stalls for current menus and hours.

spots.name: Char Koay Teow
spots.description: Flat rice noodles fried with beansprouts, prawns, cockles and egg over a fierce flame for that "wok hei" flavour.

spots.name: Penang Cendol
spots.description: A cold dessert with green jelly noodles, coconut milk, palm sugar and shaved ice — the perfect antidote to hot weather.

spots.name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
spots.description: Simple yet delicious Hainanese chicken rice, easily found in coffee shops around George Town.

spots.name: Nyonya Kuih
spots.description: A variety of colourful traditional kuih reflecting Penang's Baba Nyonya heritage.

spots.name: Wantan Mee
spots.description: Yellow noodles with greens, wantan dumplings, and roast pork or chicken.

etiquette.title: Visitor Etiquette
etiquette.intro: Chew Jetty is a living waterfront neighbourhood on Weld Quay in George Town, Penang. Explore the public wooden walkways while respecting the stilt homes and residents.
items: Treat the jetty as a residential neighbourhood; keep the atmosphere calm, especially in the early morning and late evening.
Do not take photos of residents personally, inside their homes, or of personal belongings without permission.
Do not enter residents' homes or private yards; stay on public walkways.
Dispose of rubbish in the bins provided and take your own rubbish with you.
Wooden walkways can be slippery after rain — walk carefully and wear suitable shoes.
At the shrine, avoid noise and follow local customs and taboos.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: Quick answers to common questions before you visit Chew Jetty.

items.question: What are Chew Jetty's opening hours?
items.answer: Google Maps lists 09:00–21:00 except Thursday, 09:00–21:30 (checked 19 October 2026). The tourism directory for the wider Clan Jetties area lists 11:00–21:00 daily. These sources cover different scopes; check the exact listing and on-site signs before visiting.

items.question: Is Chew Jetty open to the public?
items.answer: Visitors can use the public routes subject to posted hours and local restrictions. This is an occupied residential community; do not enter private homes or assume overnight access.

items.question: How much does it cost to enter Chew Jetty?
items.answer: Google Maps lists general admission as free. Food, souvenirs, guided experiences and other services may have their own charges.

items.question: How much time should I spend at Chew Jetty?
items.answer: Plan a flexible short visit, with extra time for photos or refreshments. The suggested 1–2 hours is a planning estimate.

items.question: Is there parking near Chew Jetty?
items.answer: Check marked bays or private car parks around Weld Quay. Rates, availability and restrictions vary; confirm signs and payment instructions on arrival.

items.question: How do I get to Chew Jetty from Penang Airport?
items.answer: Use a taxi or e-hailing service to Chew Jetty, Weld Quay, or check current Rapid Penang airport routes and connections. Journey time and fares vary.

items.question: Do I need to respect residential areas?
items.answer: Yes. Stay on public paths, keep noise low and ask before photographing people or homes. Follow barriers and instructions from residents.

items.question: Can I watch the sunset at Chew Jetty?
items.answer: Choose a late-afternoon visit for changing light over the waterfront. A clear sunset view depends on weather, viewpoint and permitted access.
